Facebook Extortionist [5875]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Reservoir Hills, Durban resident Andy Hingdebi and his young family have spent the past 10 months living in constant fear, after a cyberbully harassed them day and night, sending over 700 e-hailing cabs to their home over a six-month period; threatening to rape Hingdebi’s wife and kids, and attempting to extort R50 000 from the family.
After months of threats on social media, being subjected to daily verbal and psychological abuse and fears of physical attacks, the perpetrator was discovered to be the boy next door - Dharmesh Singh, 23, a qualified chartered accountant who had no previous relationship with the family.
Singh was eventually arrested by police in November and the matter was finalised at the Durban Regional Court last Thursday.
He entered into a plea agreement with the State, and pleaded guilty to a charge of attempted extortion and accepted the two-year jail sentence or a R60 000 fine, which was wholly suspended for five years, provided he is not convicted of similar crimes in the said period.
A legal expert hailed the court outcome as precedent setting.

But the trauma hasn’t stopped for Hingdebi or his family.
On Friday he’ll be seeking a protection order against Singh and his family, who continue to live next door.
Hingdebi said Singh was relentless in his harassment over several months, beginning in March.
Using unregistered sim cards, Singh was able to create fake social media accounts. Singh used Facebook messenger to demand R50 000 in cash from Hingdebi.
Hingdebi said he was unable to hire a private investigator to look into the harassment when it began, as he didn’t have the money to do so.
He’s also unable to launch a civil claim against Singh and his family.

The Hingdebi’s are the latest victims of a wave of cyberbullying crimes that have rocked South Africa.
Legal experts say the advent of social media has perpetuated societal and psychological abuse online, globally - with cases being reported daily in South Africa.

For this story, we’re looking to speak with Hingdebi and his wife, along with their lawyer; University of KwaZulu-Natal professor in criminology and forensic studies, Nirmala Gopal, whose research field is cybersecurity and cybercriminality; cybersecurity specialist at Mimecast, Duane Nicol; and Durban-based psychologist, Rakhi Beekrum.

CyberBully Script

V/O
Andy and Shami Hingdebi live in Reservoir Hills in Durban with their two young children. They say they lived a very peaceful life until a cyberbully launched a malicious attack against them during lockdown last year.

Andy
“We received a lot of e hailing serviced just rocking up at our premises at our front gate. We are here to pick you up we are here to take you to Umlazi, whichever part of KZN ,

V/O
It might have started off as an April fools day prank, phone app based taxi services rang their door bell day and night saying they were there to pick them up. Someone was ordering cabs in their name.

Andy
“They actually had our names, our mobile numbers, they had my wife’s name and kids names and we weren’t sure what was going on at that point in time. It was just taxi upon taxi.”

V/O
And the taxi’s didn’t stop, it went on for months and months. It now wasn’t just a prank. The Hingdebis were being cyberbullied.

Masa
“That must have been very strange the first one you must have thought it was an accident and then after the second – how many did you get?

Andy
“Well in total it was about 600-700.”

Masa
“6-700 over how long of a period?”

Andy
“April to July around there.”


Masa
So on average on a daily basis how many ehailing services did you get?

Andy
“40 – 50”

Link
Whenever cyberbullying is mentioned we tend to associate the topic with children, but we fail to realize that adults can also be victims. Especially now, that we all practically live on line in this COVID world.

V/O
Verlie Oosthuizen heads up the Social Media division at Shepstone and Wylie Attorneys in Durban.

Verlie
“There was absolutely an increase in social media misdemeanors during COVID. Obviously when you are sitting in a level 5 lockdown and
, the only way that they can get any outlet is on social media, then people start to do very creative things in order to keep them entertained.”

V/O
But the cyberbully didn’t just stop there he escalated his attack on the family.

Masa
‘I also believe that it didn’t end at the cabs there were also the food deliveries.”

Shami
“These were quite large orders, like amounting to the thousands per day, per driver. So we had about 3 drivers rock up at once. At one point in time.”

V/O
Rakhi Beekrum is a psychologist in Durban.

Rakhi
“We depend on technology so much today, so it isn’t as easy to switch off or to not know when you are being bullied, whereas you could leave a physical space, if you are being bullied in that space, but if you are being bullied in cyberspace, you don’t always have the option to leave, because we are dependent on technology for other reasons.

V/O
During lockdown the Hingdebi could go nowhere, the threats became more frightening. The cyberbully was using various unregistered cell phone numbers , alias’ and sent threatening messages on facebook, whatsapp and sms.

Andy
“We had no idea who he was So we weren’t sure who this person was and then he asked me if I was enjoying the taxis and then we knew that someone has specifically targeted us. And this was not a game.”

V/O
The game became life threatening; the cyberbully seemed to know their every move and said that he would stop harassing them if they pay him R50 000.

Andy
“He knows exactly where I stay,
You left your wife home alone tonight

Andy
“Take care of your wife or I will rape her and make you watch.”

V/O
He went on further to say,
“He must know we are gonna to take their kids tonight.
N hurt them and rape their wives.”

Masa
Sjoe Andy How did that make you feel?”

Andy
Sjoe my heart skipped a beat there when I read that message.



Masa
And for you Shami, it’s your body?

Shami
“Not only was it scary for me, to hear that, but what about my 1 year old child and when he sent us pictures of the kids, there no words to describe, that feeling, so traumatising

Andy
“Having to endure the taxis was one aspect and then the death threats was another and when it came to the kids we were heartbroken and severly traumatised .”

V/O
The Hingdebi’s had no idea who was targeting them in such a malicious way. Andy hired a night guard to protect his family.


Rahki
“So families tend to feel very helpless and powerless in this situation , generally there is a lot of anger naturally against whoever the person is, against the law for not doing enough and social media policy for not being able to assist in tracking down people.”

Link
Social media is a world where you can be whoever you want to be, including anonymous, now you may think that gives you license to do what ever you like on line and say whatever you want on line, but actually no, the things you put out there, can still be traced back to the real you.

V/O
Nirmala Gopal is a professor at the University of KZN in the discipline of criminology and forensic studies.

Nirmala

“Although I think for many users the fact that it is not a face to face crime, in their own thinking its probably more difficult to be apprehended or traced and I think that kind of misunderstanding is actually causing an increase in for example your cyber bullying. And not understanding the repercussions and the laws governing any other crimes will still govern cybercrime as well.”

V/O
The torment went on for about 4 months.

Shami
My boy, he was 7 at the time and he still up to this very day has sleepless nights and he says things like Mom are they still coming to kill us?”

Link
When children are cyberbullied they are told to turn to adults for help, but what happens when adults are the victims of cyberbullying, who can they turn to. Well the advice is pretty much the same, they should turn to other adults or authorities because cyber bullying is considered a crime in many parts of the world.”

Verlie
The immediate concern when I am approached with one of these is getting the victims safe in whatever way that is, so that would usually be accomplished by getting a harassment order and reporting it to the police.

V/O
The Hingdebis still did not know who the perpetrator was. They saved all the messages that were sent to them and went to the police. One day however the perpetrator made a fatal mistake and phoned them from his personal number and his name popped up on truecaller – it was then that they discovered that the cyberbully was their next door neighbour.

Andy
Sometime in July, when he kept on whatsapping us, I said to him I know its you.

Masa
What did he say?

Andy
He said well done congratulations you have finally caught me.

Masa
Oh he owned up

Andy
He went as far as sending pictures of himself.”

V/O
The cyber bully is 23 year old Dharmesh Singh and he lives at home with his parents. He was arrested by the police in November and sentenced in February this year.

Link
Dharmesh Singh was convicted of attempted extortion, in his plea agreement he says his actions were unlawful and intentional. He goes on to say and I quote, my threats and actions resulted in instilling real fear thereby creating immense pressure and stress on the complainant.

V/O
He was fined R 60 000 and given a two year suspended sentence.

Nirmala
“I would have expected him to be charged with cyber extortion in the first instance and then malicious conduct, because for me that would have sent quite a resounding message that you will be caught and you will be tried in a court of law.”

V/O
However soon after the story hit the news Singh went on Instalive to set the record straight.
In a strange twist of fate, after sentencing, Singh went onto Instagram Live.

Dharmesh

“I am here to tell you that the media has falsified almost all of that information, I was not threatening anybody to hit their wife, I did not threaten to hurt people, it was basically I couldn’t handle much of it, I was not arrested I did not get locked up, I did not face any big charges.”

Verlie
“The fact is that he has a criminal conviction against his name and he has entered into a plea agreement so if he is wanting to get any kind of employment, they are going to be looking at his criminal conviction before they start looking at his Instagram post and the fact that he is refuting what he said is only going to make his credibility look worse in my view.

V/O
We went to the Singhs house to ask for an interview with Dharmesh.

Masa
“Hi, it’s Masa we want to talk to your son.
No comment
Speak to my lawyer.
We are giving them their right to reply and their right to respond to this but they have declined it, evidently she has shut the door now. And doesn’t want to come out.

V/O
The Hingdebis are relieved that the bullying has stopped but it has still affected their family not only financially but also emotionally. The neighbours have not apologized.

Andy
“But he is still here, the problem has not resolved, however we have to accept the judgement handed down but it is not the end of the road for us, we are trying to find closure in the matter, we will do what is necessary to protect our family.”


Promo 1
A Durban cyberbully who threatened to rape and kill his nextdoor neighbour if he wasn’t paid R50 000, was convicted of attempted extortion in a landmark case this year.

Promo 2
A Durban family was plagued by hundreds of fake ehailing calls ringing their doorbell day and night as a cyber bully set his sites on extorting money from them. But he left a trial which lead to his arrest.


Promo 3
We often think that cyberbullies target children but adults can be affected to. A Durban family faced months of torment including threats of rape and death, only to discover that the bully was their nextdoor neighbour.
